newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - TELEBRAS TARGET PRICE SET.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - TELEBRAS TARGET PRICE SET.

text.p: HSBC James Capel said Monday it set a target price for Brazil's federal telecoms holding Telebras of between $168 and $189 after the government sold two more B Band cellular concessions.
-- HSBC James Capel analyst Paul Aran said in a report the target price was based on asset valuation and concluded 15 percent of the Telebras system's value comes from cellular operations.
-- "The entire telebras system is valued at $89.6 billion, $12.6 billion for cellular and $77 billion for wire-line," Aran wrote.
-- Telebras owns 80 percent in its subsidiaries and its stock should trade at a 10 percent to 20 percent discount "depending on market euphoria surrounding the privatization process," he said.
-- The target price represents an upside potential of 22 percent to 37 percent from current levels, he added.

-- He said Telebras' Sao Paulo state unit Telesp should sell at a premium on a per-inhabitant basis to the B Band concessions for the same area because it already has network infrastructure in place and a surscriber base.

-- On Friday, the government sold the B Band license for Sao Paulo state for 1.3 billion reais ($1.2 billion) and last month sold the concession for Sao Paulo city for 2.64 billion reais ($2.5 billion).
-- HSBC James Capel set a target price of $465 for Telesp and $269 for Telerj.
-- Telebras preferred closed down 1.8 percent at 147 reais in Sao Paulo. Its ADR ended off 3n11 at 134n01 in New York.
